layout_details.content: # INTRODUCTION
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The common ISO/IEC dictionary schema presented here is based on the intersection of the scopes of the following standards:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Relevant parts of the scope clauses of these standards include the following:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: "This part of IEC 61360 provides a firm basis for the clear and unambiguous definition of characteristic properties (data element types) of all elements of electrotechnical systems from basic components to subassemblies and full systems. Although originally conceived in the context of providing a basis for the exchange of information on electric/electronic components, the principles and methods of this standard may be used in areas outside the originalconception such as assemblies of components and electrotechnical systems and subsystems."
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: "This part of ISO 13584 specifies the principles to be used for defining characterization classes of parts and properties of parts which provide for characterizing a part independently of any particular supplier-defined identification.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The rules and guidelines provided in this part of ISO 13584 are mandatory for the standardization committees responsible for creating standardized characterization hierarchies.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The use of these rules by suppliers and users is recommended as a methodology for building their own hierarchies."
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IEC SC3D and ISO TC184/SC4 agreed NOT to change and/or modify the presented EXPRESS model independent of each other in order to guarantee the harmonization and the reusability of the work from both committees. Requests for amendments should therefore be sent to both committees. These requests should be adopted by both committees before modifying the EXPRESS information model
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # STANDARD DATA ELEMENT TYPES WITH ASSOCIATED CLASSIFICATION SCHEME FOR ELECTRIC COMPONENTS-
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Part 2: EXPRESS dictionary schema
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 1 Scope
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This part of IEC 61360 series provides a formal model for data according to the scope as given in IEC 61360-1 and ISO 13584-42, and thus provides a means for the computer-sensible representation and exchange of such data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The intention is to provide a common information model for the work of IEC SC3D and ISO TC184/SC4, thus allowing for the implementation of dictionary systems dealing with data delivered according to either of the standards elaborated by both committees.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The scope of this part of IEC 61360 is the common ISO/IEC dictionary schema based on the intersection of the scopes of the two base standards IEC 61360-1 and ISO 13584-42.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The presented EXPRESS model represents a common formal model for the two standards and facilitates a harmonization of both.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The IEC 61360-2 forms the master document. ISO 13584-42 contains a copy of the IEC 61360-2 EXPRESS model in an informative annex
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In a number of clauses, where the common EXPRESS model allows more freedom, IEC has defined more restrictions which are found in the methodology part of IEC 61360-1.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Two schemas are provided in this part of IEC 61360 defining the two options that may be selected for an implementation. Each of these options is referred to as a conformance class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - The ISO13584_IEC61360_dictionary_schema2 provides for modelling and exchanging technical data element types with associated classification scheme used in the data element type definitions. It constitutes conformance class 1 of this part of IEC 61360.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - The ISO13584_IEC61360_language_resource_schema provides resources for permitting strings in various languages. It has been extracted from the dictionary schema, since it could be used in other schemata. It is largely based on the support_resource_schema from ISO 10303-41:2000, and can be seen as an extension to that. It allows for the usage of one specific language throughout an exchange context (physical file) without the overhead introduced when multiple languages are used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When used together with ISO 10303-21, each schema defines one single exchange format. The exchange format defined by conformance class 1 is fully compatible with the ISO 13584 series.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO 13584-26:2000, Industrial automation systems and integration - Parts library - Part 26: Logical resource: Information supplier identification
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO 13584-42:2010, Industrial automation systems and integration - Parts library - Part 42: Description methodology: Methodology for structuring parts families
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 3 Terms and definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For the purposes of this document, the following terms and definitions apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: abstract class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: class of which all members are also members of one of its subclasses
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Abstract classes are used when it is needed to group different kinds of objects in a class of a class inclusion hierarchy.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, both abstract categorization classes and abstract characterization classes can be defined. The fact of being abstract is only a conceptual characteristic of a class. This characteristic is not explicitly represented in the model.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: Through inheritance, abstract characterization class allows to share, for example, some visible properties between different subclasses that correspond to different kinds of items.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## applicable property of a class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: applicable property necessarily possessed by each part that is member of a characterization class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Each part that is member of a characterization class possesses an aspect corresponding to each applicable property of this characterization class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: The above definition is conceptual, there is no requirement that all the applicable properties of a class should be used for describing each part of this class at the data model level.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: All the applicable properties of a superclass are also applicable properties for the subclasses of this superclass.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: Only properties defined or inherited as visible and imported properties of a class may be applicable properties.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: To facilitate integration of component libraries and electronic catalogues based on ISO 13584-24:2003 and ISO 13584-25, these parts of ISO 13584 request that only properties that are applicable to a class be used to characterize their instances in component libraries and electronic catalogues.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## attribute
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: data element for the computer-sensible description of a property, a relation or a class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: An attribute describes only one single detail of a property, of a class or of a relation.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The name of a property, the code of a class, the measure unit in which values of a property are provided.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## basic semantic unit
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: entity that provides an absolute and universally unique identification of a certain object of the application domain that is represented as a dictionary element
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 A dictionary compliant with this part of IEC 61360 provides for the identification of classes, properties, information sources and datatypes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 A dictionary compliant with ISO 13584-24:2003 provides for the identification of classes, properties, information sources, datatypes, tables, documents and program libraries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 In ISO 13584-511, the class of the hexagon head bolts is identified by a BSU, the property thread tolerance grade is also identified by a BSU.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: The content of a basic semantic unit may also be represented as an IRDI.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## characteristic of a product
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## product characteristic
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: invariable property, characteristic of a product, whose value is fixed once the product is defined
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Changing the value of a characteristic of a product would mean changing the product.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE For a ball bearing, the inner diameter and the outer diameter are product characteristics.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Adapted from ISO 13584-24:2003, definition 3.12.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: abstraction of a set of similar products
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: A product that complies with the abstraction defined by a class is called a class member.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: A class is an intentional concept that can take different extensional meanings in different contexts.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The set of products used by a particular enterprise and the set of all ISO-standardized products are two examples of contexts. In these two contexts (the particular enterprise and ISO), the set of products that are considered as members of the single ball bearing class can be different, in particular because employees of each enterprise ignore a number of existing single ball bearing products.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: Classes are structured by class inclusion relationships.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: A class of products is a general concept as defined in ISO 1087-1. Thus, it is advisable that the rules defined in ISO 704 be used for defining the designation and definition attributes of classes of products.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: In the context of the ISO 13584 series, a class is either a characterization class, associated with properties and usable for characterizing products, or a categorization class, not associated with properties and not usable for characterizing products.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## class inclusion relationship
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: relationship between classes that means inclusion of class members: if A is a superclass of A1 this means that, in any context, any member of A1 is also member of A
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 The set of products used by a particular enterprise and the set of all ISO-standardized products are two examples of contexts.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 In any context, the class capacitor includes the class electrolytic capacitor.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Class inclusion defines a hierarchical structure between classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Class inclusion is a conceptual relationship that does not prescribe anything at the data representation level. Consequently, it does not prescribe any particular database schema or data model.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: In the model defined in this part of IEC 61360, the "is-a" relationship ensures class inclusion. This part of IEC 61360 recommends that the "case-of" relationship also ensure class inclusion.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: The class inclusion relationship is also called subsumption.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## class member
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: product that complies with the abstraction defined by a class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## class valued property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: property that has one single value for a whole characterization class of products
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: The value of a class valued property is not defined individually for every single product of a characterization class, but globally for the class itself.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: When all products from a characterization class of products have the same value for a particular property, defining this property as a class valued property permits to avoid duplication of the value for each instance.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: Class valued properties can also be used to capture some commonality between different characterization classes when such a commonality is not captured by the hierarchy structure.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: data model for product ontology, using the information modeling language EXPRESS resulting from a joint effort between ISO/TC 184/SC 4/WG 2 and IEC SC3D
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Several levels of allowed implementations, known as conformance classes, are defined for the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model. Conformance class 1 consists of the various schemes documented
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: in this part of IEC 61360 (that duplicate information contained in this standard), more the ISO13584_IEC61360_dictionary_aggregate_extension_schema documented in ISO 13584-25 (duplicated in IEC 61360-5). Other conformance classes are documented in ISO 13584-25 (conformance classes 2, 3 and 4).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: In the ISO 13584 standard series, each particular product ontology addressing a particular product domain and based on the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model is called a reference dictionary for that domain.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## context dependent characteristic of product
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: property of a product whose value depends on some context parameters
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: For a given product, a context dependent characteristic is mathematically defined as a function whose domain is defined by some context parameters that define the product environment.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE For a ball bearing, the life-time is a context dependent characteristic that depends on the radial load the axial load and the rotational speed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Adapted from ISO 13584-24:2003, definition 3.22.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## context parameter
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: variable whose value characterizes the context in which a product is inserted
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 The dynamic-load applied to a bearing is a context parameter for this bearing.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 The ambient temperature in which the resistance of a resistor is measured is a context parameter for this resistor.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This definition supersedes the definition given in ISO 13584-24:2003, that was the following: "a variable of which the value characterizes the context in which it is intended to insert a product".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: In the ISO 13584 standard series, a property value is represented as a data element type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## data element type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: unit of data for which the identification, description and value representation have been specified
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In the ISO 13584 standard series, a property value is represented as a data element type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## dictionary data
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: set of data that represents product ontologies possibly associated with product categorizations
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: It is advisable that dictionary data be exchanged using some conformance class of the common ISO/IEC dictionary model.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: This definition of dictionary data supersedes the previous definition from the first edition of IEC 61360-2 that was the following: "the set of data that describes hierarchies of characterization classes of products and properties of these products".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## dictionary element
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: set of attributes that constitutes the dictionary description of certain objects of the application domain
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 A dictionary compliant with this part of IEC 61360 provides for the description of classes, properties, information sources and datatypes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 A dictionary compliant with ISO 13584-24:2003 provides for the description of classes, properties, information sources, datatypes, tables, documents and program libraries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## family of products
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: set of products represented by the same characterization class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This definition supersedes the definition given in ISO 13584-24:2003, that was the following: "a simple or generic family of parts".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## feature
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: aspect of a product that can be described by a characterization class and a set of property-value pairs
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In the real world, a feature instance only exists embedded within the product of which it is an aspect.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 The head of a screw is a feature described by a head class and a number of head properties, which depends upon the head class. A screw head only exists when it belongs to a screw.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Features are represented by means of item_class whose the instance_sharable attribute equals false.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: The instance_sharable attribute allows to specify the conceptual status of an item: either a stand-alone item (instance_sharable =true), or a feature (instance_sharable =false). It does not imply any constraint at the data representation level. In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, representing several real world instances that share the same EXPRESS representation by a single EXPRESS entity, or by several EXPRESS entities is considered as implementation dependant. There exist no mechanism for specifying whether data value of a feature instance may or may not be shared.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 The same instance of a screw head class can be referenced by several instances of a screw class. It means that there exists several screw heads, but that all these screw heads have the same characterization class and the same set of property values. The instance_sharable attribute allows to specify that changing this instance of the screw head class would change several instances of the screw class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## imported property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: property defined in a class that is selected by another class of the same or of a different reference dictionary, by means of the case-of relationship, to become applicable to the latter class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Only properties that are visible and/or applicable in a class can be imported from this class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Importation between classes of different reference dictionaries allows reusing properties, defined for example in a standard reference dictionary, without redefining them.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: Importation between classes of the same reference dictionary acknowledges the fact that some products can perform several functions, requiring the capability to import property from several higher level classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: When it is imported in a new class, a property keeps its original identifier, thus all the attributes do not need to be duplicated.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: An imported property is applicable for the class where it is imported.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: information
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: facts, concepts or instructions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [SOURCE: ISO 10303-1:1994, definition 3.2.20]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: information model
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: formal model of a bounded set of facts, concepts or instructions to meet a specified requirement
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [SOURCE: ISO 10303-1:1994, definition 3.2.21]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: information supplier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: supplier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: organization that delivers an ontology, i.e. a data dictionary, or a supplier library that is responsible for its content
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This definition of supplier supersedes the definition of information supplier from ISO 13584-1:2001 that was the following: "organization that delivers a supplier library in the standard format defined in this International Standard and is responsible for its content".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## international registration data identifier
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: internationally unique identifier for a certain object of the application domain as defined in ISO/IEC 11179-5
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Only international registration data identifiers compliant with ISO/TS 29002-5 are used in the context of the ISO 13584 standard series.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: An international registration data identifier may be used for representing the content of a basic semantic unit that identifies a dictionary element as a string.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: An international registration data identifier may also be used for identifying the content of an attribute of a dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The unit of measure of a property, a value of a property or a constraint over a property may be identified by an IRDI.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## is-a relationship
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: class inclusion relationship associated with inheritance: if A1 is-a A, then each product belonging to A1 belongs to A, and all that is described in the context of A is automatically duplicated in the context of A1
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This mechanism is usually called "inheritance".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, the is-a relationship can only be defined between characterization classes. It is advisable that it defines a single hierarchy and it ensures that both visible and applicable properties are inherited.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## is-case-of relationship
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## case-of
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: property importation mechanism: if A1 is case-of A, then the definition of A products also covers A1 products, thus A1 can import any property from A
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: The goal of the case-of relationship is to allow connecting together several class inclusion hierarchies while ensuring that referenced hierarchies can be updated independently.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: There is no constraint that the case-of relationship is intended to define single hierarchies.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, the case-of relationship can in particular be used in four cases: (1) to link a characterization class to a categorization class, (2) to import, in the context of some standardized reference dictionaries, some properties already defined in other standardized reference dictionaries, (3) to connect a user reference dictionary to one or several standardized reference dictionaries, (4) to describe a product using the properties of different classes: when products of class A1 fulfil two different functions, and are thus logically described by properties associated with two different classes, A and B, A1 can be connected by is-a to e. g., A, and by case-of to B.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: The EXPRESS resource constructs for modeling the case-of relationships are defined in 4.5 and after.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## item
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: thing that can be characterized by means of a characterization class to which it belongs and a set of property value pairs
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This definition supersedes the definition given in ISO 13584-24:2003, that was the following: "a thing that can be captured by a class structure and a set of properties".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: In the ISO 13584 standard series, both products and features of products that correspond to composite properties are items.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## leaf characterization class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: characterization class that is not further specialized into more precise characterization classes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Countersunk flat head screw with cross recess (type Y) and hexagon socket head cap screw with metric fine pitch thread are leaf characterization classes defined in ISO 13584-511.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## non-leaf characterization class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: characterization class that is further specialized into more precise characterization classes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Externally-threaded component and metric threaded bolt/screw are non-leaf characterization classes defined in ISO 13584-511.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## non-quantitative data element type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: data element type that identifies or describes an object by means of codes, abbreviations names, references or descriptions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## part
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: material or functional element that is intended to constitute a component of different products
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [SOURCE: ISO 13584-1:2001, definition 3.1.16]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## parts library
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: computer-sensible product ontology and computer-sensible description of a set of products by means of references to this ontology
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This definition supersedes the definition given in the first edition of this part of IEC 61360, which was the following: "identified set of data and possibly programs which can generate information about a set of parts".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## product
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: thing or substance produced by a natural or artificial process
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In this part of IEC 61360, the term product is taken in its widest sense to include devices, systems and installations as well as materials, processes, software and services.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## product categorization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## part categorization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## categorization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: recursive partition of a set of products into subsets for a specific purpose
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Subsets which appear in a product categorization are called product categorization classes, or product categories.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: A product categorization is not a product ontology. It cannot be used for characterizing products.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: No property is associated with categorizations.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: Several categorizations of the same set of products are possible according to their target usage.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The UNSPSC classification, defined by the United Nations, is an example of a product categorization that was developed for spend analysis.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: Using the is-case-of relationship, several product characterization class hierarchies can be connected to a categorization hierarchy to generate a single structure.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: class of products that constitutes an element of a categorization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Manufacturing Components and Supplies, and Industrial Optics are examples of a product categorization class defined in the UNSPSC.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: No rule is given in this part of IEC 61360 about how to select categorization classes. This concept is introduced (1) to clarify its difference with characterization class, and (2) to explain that the same characterization class can be connected to any number of categorization classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: There is no property associated with a categorization class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## product characterization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: part characterization
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: description of a product by means of a product characterization class to which it belongs and a set of property value pairs
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Hexagon_head_bolts_ISO_4014 (Product grades = A, thread_type=M, length= 50, Diameter = 8) is an example of a product characterization.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: class of products that fulfil the same function and that share common properties
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Product characterization classes can be defined at various levels of details, thus defining a class inclusion hierarchy.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE Metric threaded bolt/screw and hexagon head bolt are examples of product characterization classes defined in ISO 13584-511. The first characterization class is included in the second one. Transistor and bipolar power transistor are examples of product characterization classes defined in IEC 61360-DB. The second one is included in the first one.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## product ontology
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: model of product knowledge, done by a formal and consensual representation of the concepts of a product domain in terms of identified characterization classes, of class relations and of identified properties
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Product ontologies are based on a class-instance model that allows one to recognize and to designate the sets of products, called characterization classes, that have a similar function (e.g., ball bearing, capacitor), but also to discriminate within a class the various subsets of products, called instances, that are considered as identical. It is advisable that the rules defined in ISO 1087-1 be used for formulating designation and definitions of characterization classes. Instances have no definitions. They are designated by the class to which they belong, and a set of property-value pairs.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Ontologies are not concerned with words but with concepts, independent of any particular language.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: "Consensual" means that the conceptualization is agreed upon in some community.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: "Formal" means that the ontology is intended to be machine interpretable. Some level of machine reasoning is logically possible over ontology, e.g., consistency checking, making inferences.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: "Identified" means that each ontology characterization class and properties are associated with a globally unique identifier allowing one to reference this concept from any context.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 6 to entry: The data model for ontology recommended in this part of IEC 61360 is the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, whose simplest version is documented in this part of IEC 61360. More complete versions are documented in ISO 13584-25 and IEC 61360-5 (conformance classes 1, 2, 3 and 4 of both documents).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 7 to entry: In this part of IEC 61360, each product ontology addressing a particular product domain compliant with the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model is called a reference dictionary for that domain.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The reference dictionary for electric components, which is defined in IEC 61360-DB, is a product ontology for electric components compliant with the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model. It is agreed upon by all member bodies of IEC SC3D. A corporate reference dictionary is agreed upon by experts designated by management on behalf of the company.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: defined parameter suitable for the description and differentiation of products
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: A property describes one aspect of a given object.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: A property is defined by the totality of its associated attributes. The types and number of attributes that describe a property with high accuracy are documented in this part of IEC 61360.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: This part of IEC 61360 has identified three different kinds of properties: product characteristics, context parameters and context-dependent product characteristics.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: This definition of property supersedes the previous definition of the previous edition of this part of IEC 61360 that was the following: "an information that can be represented by a data element type".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: In the ISO 13584 standard series, a property value is represented as a data element type.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## property data type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: allowed set of values of a property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## property definition class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: product characterization class in the context of which a product property is defined
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, each product property has one property definition class that defines its domain of application. The property is only meaningful for this class, and all its subclasses, and it is said to be visible over this domain.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE In ISO 13584-511, wrenching height has nut as its property definition class and major diameter of external thread has metric external thread as its property definition class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## quantitative data element type
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: data element type with a numerical value representing a physical quantity, a quantity of information or a count of objects
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## reference dictionary
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: product ontology compliant with the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In the ISO 13584 standard series, a product ontology that addresses a particular product domain, based on the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, is called a reference dictionary for that domain.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## resource construct
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: collection of EXPRESS language entities, types, functions, rules and references that together define a valid description of data
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: This definition is adapted from the definition of resource construct in ISO 10303-1:1994, i.e., "the collection of EXPRESS language entities, types, functions, rules and references that together define a valid description of product data".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: [SOURCE: ISO 13584-1:2001, definition 3.1.21, modified]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## subclass
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: class that is one step below another class in a class inclusion hierarchy
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, class inclusion hierarchies are defined by the is-a relationship. They can also be established by the case-of relationships.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## superclass
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: class that is one step above another class in a class inclusion hierarchy
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, class inclusion hierarchies are defined by the is-a relationship. They can also be established by the case-of relationships.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: In the common ISO13584/IEC61360 dictionary model, a class has at most one superclass specified by means of an is-a relationship.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## supplier library
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: parts library of which the information supplier is different from the library user
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: This definition supersedes the definition given in ISO 13584-1:2001, that was the following: "set of data, and possibly of programs, for which the supplier is defined and that describes in the standard format defined in this International Standard a set of products and/or a set of representation of products".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## visible property
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: property that has a definition meaningful in the scope of a given characterization class, but that does not necessarily apply to the various products belonging to this class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Meaningful in the scope of a given characterization class means that a human observer is able to determine, for any product of the characterization class, whether the property applies, and, if it applies, to which product aspect it corresponds.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: The concept of a visible property allows sharing the definition of a property among product characterization classes where this property does not necessarily apply.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The non-threaded length property is meaningful for any class of screw but it applies only to those screws that have a non-threaded part. It can be defined as visible at the screw level, while becoming applicable only in some subclasses.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 3 to entry: All the visible properties of a superclass that is a product characterization class are also visible properties for its subclasses.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 4 to entry: To facilitate integration of component libraries and electronic catalogues based on ISO 13584-24:2003 and ISO 13584-25, these parts of ISO 13584 request that only properties that are applicable to a class be used to characterize their instances in component libraries and electronic catalogues.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 5 to entry: This definition of a visible property supersedes the previous definition from ISO 13584-24:2003 that was the following: "a property that is defined for some class of products and that does not necessarily apply to the different products of this class of products".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4 Overview of the common dictionary schema and compatibility with ISO13584_IEC61360_dictionary_schema
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In the following subclauses the architecture of the common dictionary schema will be presented and it will be explained how the same information model has to be used in the International Standards to ensure their compatibility.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The common dictionary schema combines the requirements of IEC 61360 series and ISO 13584 series. Therefore, it contains resources to accommodate the specific requirements of both series of International Standards. These resources are provided either as optional capabilities or as subtypes of the types defined to fulfil the common requirements.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.2 Use of the common dictionary schema to exchange IEC 61360-1 compliant data
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The common dictionary schema to exchange IEC 61360-1 compliant data shall be used as follows:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) the ISO 13584 series specific extensions to support multilingual capability are not required for the exchange of dictionary elements defined according to IEC 61360-1. However these extensions that are present translations, translated_label and translated_text shall be used in the exchange structure for compatibility reasons;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) if a component class has a superclass, the coded_name shall be defined as a value_code in the domain of the classifying data element type of the superclass;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: c) if a classifying data element type exists within a specific component class, for each value in its domain a subclass and a term shall be defined;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: d) a classifying data element type, optional in conformance class 2 in the common dictionary schema, shall always be provided for the component classes defined according to IEC 61360-1;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: e) only SI units shall be used although the common dictionary schema enables the use of many kind of system units. When using this schema however for the exchange of IEC 61360 series compliant data, only SI shall be used for quantitative data element types.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.3 Compatibility with ISO 13584-42
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An implementation compliant with this part of IEC 61360 shall support all the entities, types and associated constraints that belong to the conformance class it claims to support. Therefore conformance to conformance class 1 of this part of IEC 61360 requires that all the entities, types and associated constraints defined in the common dictionary schema be supported. ISO 13584 data conforming to the common dictionary schema may thus be processed by an IEC 61360 implementation that conforms to conformance class 1 that includes all the features of conformance class 1. In ISO 13584, a specific conformance class 3 is intended to contain all the entities, types and associated constraints defined in the common dictionary schema. An ISO 13584 compliant implementation conforms to this conformance class shall therefore be able to support IEC data that belongs to conformance class 1 of this part of IEC 61360.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 4.4 Naming correspondence between IEC 61360-1 and IEC 61360-2
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Due to specific application restrictions - for example the EXPRESS language allows no spaces in entity names -, a number of similar 'EXPRESS names' are created by replacing the blank in a name by an underscore (for example preferred name is presented as preferred_name).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: At other places names are used in the EXPRESS model that deviate from those used in IEC 61360-1. This is a consequence of the effort to reach one common EXPRESS information model together with Part Libraries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The table below presents a help for matching the names used in the two parts of IEC 61360.

layout_details.content: ## 4.5 Main structure of the common dictionary schema
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This subclause explains the main resource constructs provided by the common dictionary schema:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - dictionary_element is any element defined in the dictionary;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - supplier_element captures the data of suppliers of dictionary elements (classes, properties, data types); class models the dictionary element of classes (families) which are described by properties;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - property_DET is the dictionary element of a property;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - data_type specifies the type of a property.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: These parts of the dictionary schema are presented in more detail in clause 5: ISO13584_IEC61360_dictionary_schema.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In the presentation of the common dictionary schema, some overview diagrams are provided as planning models (see Figure 1 to Figure 11). These planning models use the EXPRESS-G graphical notation for the EXPRESS language. For clarification of the diagrams, some of the relationships that are defined in the EXPRESS model are omitted. Figure 1 below outlines as a planning model the main structure of the common dictionary schema. Most of these figures contain overview models (or planning models) but show only that level of detail which is appropriate at a certain place.

layout_details.content: ## 5.5 Identification of a dictionary
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A dictionary_identification entity allows to identify unambiguously a particular version of a particular dictionary of a particular information supplier, standard or not. It contains a code defined by the dictionary supplier that identifies the dictionary, a version number and revision number that characterize a particular state of this dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The case where dictionary version and revision should be incremented is defined in IEC 61360-1.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content:
UNIQUE

UR1: absolute_id;

END_ENTITY; -- dictionary_identification

(*
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Attribute definitions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: code: the code that characterizes the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: version: the version number that characterizes the version of the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: revision: the revision number that characterizes the revision of the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: defined_by: the supplier who defines the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: absolute_id: the unique identification of the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Formal propositions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: UR1: the dictionary identifier defined by the absolute_id attribute is unique.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Informal propositions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IP1: when a dictionary is defined by a standard document that contains only one dictionary, the dictionary code shall be the standard number of the document that describes this dictionary if this document only defines one dictionary. It shall be the name defined for the pertinent dictionary in the document that describes it if this document defines several dictionaries. Unless otherwise specified, version shall be set to 1 and revision numbers shall be set to 0 for dictionaries defined by standard documents.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Representation of the standard numbers of standard documents is specified in 5.1 and 5.2 of ISO 13584-26:2000.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6 Basic Semantic Units: defining and using the dictionary
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.1 Requirements for exchange
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In the exchange of dictionary and part library data, it is customary to partition the data. For example, a dictionary could be updated with some classes that specify their superclass by a reference to a pre-existing class, or when the content of a library is exchanged, dictionary elements are only referenced and not included every time. It shall be possible to refer unambiguously and consistently to the dictionary data.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Thus, it is a clear requirement first, to be able to exchange pieces of data, and second, to have relationships between these pieces. This is depicted in Figure 2.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 2 - Pieces of data with relationships
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Every one of these pieces corresponds to a physical file (according to ISO 10303-21). EXPRESS (ISO 10303-11:2004) attributes can only contain references to data within the same physical file. Thus it is impossible to use EXPRESS attributes directly to implement inter-piece references.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.2 Three levels architecture of the dictionary data
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.2.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In this clause the concept of basic_semantic_unit (BSU) is introduced as a means to implement these inter-piece references. A BSU provides a universally unique identification for dictionary descriptions. This is depicted in Figure 3
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Assume some piece of content wants to refer a certain dictionary description.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 To convey the value of a property of a component.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: It does this by referring to a basic semantic unit through the attribute dictionary_definition.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A dictionary description (dictionary_element) refers to a basic semantic unit through the attribute identified_by. From the correspondence of the absolute identifiers of the basic semantic units this indirect relation is established.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 3 - Implementation of "inter-piece" relationships using basic semantic units
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note that:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - both dictionary element and content item can be present in the same physical file, but need not be;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the dictionary element does not need to be present for the exchange of some content item referring to it. In this case it is assumed to be present in the dictionary of the target system already. Conversely, dictionary data can be exchanged without any content data;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the basic semantic unit can be one single instance in the case where both dictionary element and content item instances are in the same physical file;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the same mechanism applies also to references between various dictionary elements
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 Between a class of components and the associated property_DETs.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A BSU provides a reference to a dictionary description in any place where this is needed.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 3 Dictionary delivery, update delivery, library delivery, component data exchange.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The data associated with a property could be exchanged as a pair (property_BSU, <value>).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 3 outlines the implementation of this general mechanism.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.2.2 Basic_semantic_unit
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A basic semantic unit is a unique identification of a dictionary_element. BSU is the abbreviation of basic semantic unit.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: code: the code assigned to identify a certain dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: version: the version number of a certain dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: dic_identifier: the full identification, consisting of concatenation of code and version.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: definition: a reference to the dictionary element identified by this BSU. If not present in some exchange context, it is assumed to be present in the dictionary of the target system already.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: referenced_by: items making use of the dictionary element associated with this BSU.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.2.3 Dictionary_element
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A dictionary_element is a full definition of the data required to be captured in the semantic dictionary for some concepts. For every concept, a separate subtype is to be used. The dictionary_element is associated with a basic_semantic_unit (BSU) that serves to uniquely identify this definition in the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: By including the version attribute in the basic_semantic_unit entity, it forms part of the identification of a dictionary element (in contrast to the revision and time_stamps attributes).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text
text
text

layout_details.content: Attribute definitions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: identified_by: the BSU identifying this dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: time_stamps: the optional dates of creation and update of this dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: revision: the revision number of this dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 The type of the identified_by attribute will be redefined later to property_BSU and class_BSU and will then be used to encode together with the code attribute of the BSUs the "Code" attribute for properties and classes respectively. It will also be used to encode the "Version Number" attribute for properties and classes respectively.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 The time_stamps attribute will be used as a starting point to encode in the dates entity the property and class attributes "Date of Original Definition", "Date of Current Version" and "Date of Current Revision" (see 5.11.3.2).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 The revision attribute will be used to encode the property and class attribute "Revision Number".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: administration: optional information on the life cycle of the dictionary_element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 The administration attribute will be used to represent the information related to the configuration management and translation history.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is_deprecated: an optional Boolean. When true, it specifies that the dictionary_element shall no longer be used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is_deprecated_interpretation: specifies the deprecation rationale and how instance values of the deprecated element, and of its corresponding BSU, should be interpreted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Formal propositions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: WR1: when is_deprecated exists, is_deprecated_interpretation shall exist.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Informal propositions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: IP1: instance values of is_deprecated_interpretation element shall be defined at the time where deprecation decision was taken.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 4 presents a planning model of the relationship between basic semantic unit and the dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 4 - Relationship between basic semantic unit and dictionary element
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.2.4 Content_item
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A content_item is a piece of data referring to its description in the dictionary. It shall be subtyped.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: ## Attribute definitions:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: dictionary_definition: the basic semantic unit to be used for referring to the definition in the dictionary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.3 Overview of basic semantic units and dictionary elements
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For every kind of dictionary data, a pair of basic_semantic_unit and dictionary_element subtypes shall be defined. Figure 5 outlines, as a planning model, the basic semantic units (BSU) and dictionary elements defined later. Note that the relationship between BSU and dictionary elements is redefined for each type of data, so that only corresponding pairs can be related. This is not graphically depicted here, however.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Every kind of dictionary data is treated in one of the following subclauses:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - for suppliers see 5.7;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - for classes see 5.8;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - for properties / data element types see 5.9;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - for data types see 5.10.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Figure 5 - Current BSUs and dictionary elements
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.4 Identification of dictionary elements: three levels structure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The absolute identification of basic semantic units is based on the following three levels structure:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - supplier (of dictionary data);
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - supplier-defined dictionary element (any supplier-defined dictionary element defined in the model; in this document supplier-defined dictionary element are property_DET and data_type_element, but there are provisions to extend this mechanism to other items);
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - version of the supplier-defined dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An absolute identification can be achieved by concatenation of the applicable code for each level.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE The structure on this absolute identification is different from the structure defined in edition 1 of IEC 61360-2 (duplicated for convenience in ISO 13584-42:1998). In the previous edition, the absolute identification of any dictionary_element associated with a name_scope (including property_DET and data_type_element) consisted of: supplier code + class code (corresponding to the name_scope class) + dictionary element code + dictionary element version. In this edition, the class code has been removed. Thus, the dictionary element code is unique, for the same type of dictionary element, over all the classes defined by the same supplier. For existing reference dictionaries, registration authorities, maintenance authorities or standardization groups in charge of standard dictionaries should ensure this unicity, possibly by defining new codes prefixed by name_scope class codes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This identification scheme is appropriate within a multi-supplier context. If in a certain application area, only data of one single (data-) supplier are relevant, the corresponding parts of the identification, that are then constant, can be eliminated. For the purpose of exchange, however, all the levels shall be present, to avoid clashes of identifiers.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: This identification scheme is described formally in the absolute_id attribute of the xxx_BSU entities defined from 5.7 through 5.12.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.5 Extension possibilities for other types of data
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.5.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The BSU - dictionary element mechanism is very general and not limited to the four kinds of data used here (see Figure 5). This clause specifies some facilities that allow for extensions for other kinds. Depending on whether the scope of the identifier is given by a class or a supplier, the corresponding xxx_related_BSU entity has to be subtyped. It is necessary to redefine the identified_by attribute of the entity dictionary_element (as is done in 5.7.3 through 5.10 or the current kinds of data).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.5.2 Supplier_related_BSU
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The supplier_related_BSU provides for the dictionary elements to be associated with suppliers.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE For ISO 13584 series: program libraries.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: *) ENTITY supplier_related_BSU ABSTRACT SUPERTYPE SUBTYPE OF(basic_semantic_unit); END_ENTITY; -- supplier_related_BSU (*
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.5.3 Class_related_BSU
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The class_related_BSU provides for the dictionary elements to be associated with classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE For ISO 13584 tables, documents, etc.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: *) ENTITY class_related_BSU ABSTRACT SUPERTYPE SUBTYPE OF(basic_semantic_unit); END_ENTITY; -- class_related_BSU (*
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.5.4 Supplier_BSU_relationship
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The supplier_BSU_relationship is a provision for association of BSUs with suppliers.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: *) ENTITY supplier_BSU_relationship ABSTRACT SUPERTYPE; relating_supplier: supplier_element; related_tokens: SET [1:?] OF supplier_related_BSU; END_ENTITY; -- supplier_BSU_relationship (*
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: relating_supplier: the supplier_element that identifies the data supplier.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: related_tokens: the set of dictionary elements associated to the supplier identified by the relating_supplier attribute.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.6.5.5 Class_BSU_relationship
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The class_BSU_relationship entity is a provision for association of BSUs with classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXPRESS specification:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: *) ENTITY class_BSU_relationship ABSTRACT SUPERTYPE; relating_class: class; related_tokens: SET [1:?] OF class_related_BSU; END_ENTITY; -- class_BSU_relationship (*
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: relating_class: the class that identifies the dictionary element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: related_tokens: the set of dictionary elements associated to the class identified by the relating_class attribute.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: identified_by: the class_BSU identifying this class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: its_superclass: reference to the class the current one is a subclass of.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: described_by: the list of references to the additional properties available for use in the description of the products within the class, and any of its subclasses.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 A property may also be applicable to a class when this property is imported from another class through an a_priori_semantic_relationship as defined in 8.5 of this part of IEC 61360. Therefore the properties referenced by the described_by attribute do not define all the applicable properties for a class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 The list order is the presentation order of the properties suggested by the supplier.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 3 A property that is a context dependent property (context_dependent_P_DET) may become applicable to a class only if all the context parameters (condition_DET) on which its value depends are also applicable to this class. This is stated in where rule 5 (WR5).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: defined_types: the set of references to the types that can be used for various property_DETs throughout the inheritance tree descending from this class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 4 A data_type may also be applicable to a class when this data_type is imported from another class through an a_priori_semantic_relationship as defined in 8.5 of this part of IEC 61360. Therefore the data types referenced by the defined_types attribute do not define all the applicable data types for a class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: constraints: the set of constraints that restrict the target domains of values of some properties of the class to some subsets of their inherited domains of values.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 5 Each constraint in the constraints attribute should be fulfilled by class instances. Thus the constraints attribute is a conjunction of constraints.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: hierarchical_position: the coded representation of the class position in a class inclusion hierarchy to which it belongs; a hierarchical_position of a class changes when the class structure of an ontology is changed. Thus it cannot be used as a stable identifier for classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 6 This kind of coded name is used in particular in product categorization hierarchies for representing the class inclusion structure through some coding conventions.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 In UNSPSC, Manufacturing Components and Supplies has the hierarchical position 31000000, Hardware has the hierarchical position 31160000 and Bolt the hierarchical position 31161600. By convention, this representation of the hierarchical position allows to represent that Manufacturing Components and Supplies is at the first level of the hierarchy, that Hardware is at the second level of the hierarchy and is included in Manufacturing Components and Supplies and that Bolt is at the third level of the hierarchy and is included in Hardware.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: keywords: a set of keywords, possibly in several languages, allowing to search the class.

layout_details.content: ## 5.8.3 Item_class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The entity item_class enables the modeling of any type of entity of the application domain that may be captured by a characterization class defined by a class structure and a set of properties. In particular, both instances of products and instances of particular aspects of products represented as features, are mapped onto item_class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The item_class entity includes an instance_sharable attribute that specifies the conceptual status of an item. If this attribute is true, then each instance represents an independent item, otherwise it is a feature, i.e., a dependent item that has to be component of another item. This does not prescribe any specific implementation at the data representation level.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE The head of a screw is a feature described by a number of properties but that may only exist when referenced by a screw. It is represented as an item_class with the instance_sharable attribute equal to false.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 1 Two subtypes of item_class, named component_class and material_class, were defined within the dictionary model of the first edition of ISO 13584-42 and in IEC 61360-2. These subtypes are deprecated, and they are removed from this edition of IEC 61360.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE 2 Another subtype of item_class, named feature_class, was provided in ISO 13584-24:2003. This subtype is also deprecated and its usage is not recommended in new implementations of this part of IEC 61360.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 5.8.4 Categorization_class
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The categorization_class entity enables the modeling of a grouping of a set of objects that constitutes an element of a categorization.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 1 Manufacturing components and supplies, industrial optics, are example of product categorization class defined in UNSPSC.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Neither properties nor datatypes, nor constraints are associated, as visible or applicable, with such a class. Moreover, categorization_classs may not be related to each other by the is-a inheritance relationship, but they may only be related to each other through the is-case-of class relationship. A specific attribute, called categorization_class_superclasses, allows to record the categorization_classs that are superclasses of a categorization_class in a case-of hierarchy.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: NOTE Using the case-of resource constructs, item_classes may also be connected to categorization_classes.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: EXAMPLE 2 The following example shows how characterization classes and categorization classes may be connected to achieve some particular goals. A ball bearing supplier wants to design its own ontology and to make it easy to retrieve and easy to use. To achieve these goals, he/she wants to use standard properties and to be connected to standard classifications. The supplier provides only ball bearings, but some bearings are sealed, some others are not. Particular properties may be associated with sealed bearings and with not sealed bearings, but these categories do not exist as classes in standard bearing ontologies. Thus, the bearing supplier processes as follows. (1) He/she designs a proprietary ontology consisting of three characterization classes: my_bearing, my_sealed_bearings, my_non_sealed_bearing. The two latter are connected to the former by the is-a inheritance relationship, and all the properties assigned to the former are inherited by the latter. (2) To use some of the properties defined in the ISO/TS 23768-1 (to be published), the bearing supplier specifies that his/her class my_bearings is case-of the standard bearing class ball bearing defined in ISO/TS 23768-1. Through this case-of relationship, he/she may import in his/her class my_bearings the standard-defined properties: bore diameter, outside diameter, ISO tolerance class. Moreover, he/she creates those needed properties that are not defined in the standard. (3) To facilitate the retrieval of the server that display the supplier's catalogue, he/she represents a small fragment of the UNSPSC classification, and a case-of relationship between the UNSPSC class ball bearings and its own class my_bearing. The result is presented in Figure 8 below:
layout_details.label: text
